content:
devin: Heads-up — saw a regression on Qwen-7B fp8 calibration pack that spikes tail-latency under sustained chat loads. Profiling shows KV copy spends way more cycles. Repro: ded17/kvcopy-bench with live prefix use. pprof snippet below.

devin: ```text
# pprof flamegraph excerpt
cpu: 80%  kv_cache_copy
    40%  memcpy
    30%  cudaMemcpyAsync
    10%  quant_dequant
```

anya: Oof. This is after the fp8 cal step or during runtime? any change in kernel selection? :thinking_face:

devin: It's during runtime for calibrated fp8 kernels. Kernel selector picks mixed-fp8-int8 path now. The issue seems to be that kvcopy uses 32-bit copy path because alignment after quantization changed. I can share micro-bench.

marc: Can you paste the batch shape and sequence lengths? Also which driver and CUDA version? We've seen memcpy regressions on 12.1 vs 12.2.

devin: batch=8, seq=1024 prefetched prefixes ~256 averaged. driver=525.85, cuda=12.1. Host->device memcpy latency jumps when prefix>128.

sophia: Might be the fallback kernel for attention when head dim parity changes with quant packing. We added a slow path when head_dim%8!=0. Check kernel selection logs: set RUNTIME_KERNELOG=1

devin: Logs show fallback to attention_kernel_v2_slow for mistral-like shapes when using fp8 pack. Here's selector excerpt:

devin: ```text
[selector] model=Qwen-7B fp8_profile=calib_2026_03_14 kernel=attn_v2_slow reason=head_dim==99
```

anya: If kernel is slow we should try two things: 1) force int8 attention kernel to test perf 2) run a kvcopy microbench that uses cudaMemcpyAsync with pinned buffers.

devin: I ran forcing int8 kernel via env var and latency drops ~18% but quality diffs non-trivial on some prompts. KV microbench shows async/pinned halves memcpy time.

marc: That suggests two mitigation paths: add a quant packing tweak to keep alignment (pad heads) or route traffic to int8 fallback for heavy prefix workloads. Which is lower risk for rollout?

sophia: Pad-at-pack seems safe but needs changing calibration output (adds 0.5% token compute). Routing is fast to roll out with a canary.

devin: I'm prototyping pad-at-pack and a selector rule: if prefix_avg>200 -> prefer int8_fallback. Will push a config PR and a small perf test. 

infra-bot: deploy requested by devin for branch quant/pack-pad -> eng-ml-canary at 1950457000

anya: SGTM. Add a unit that verifies no quality regressions >0.5 BLEU diff on eval prompts.

devin: Will do. Plan: PR with padding + perf numbers + canary rule. Expect results by EOD. Thanks.
